node.title: Infinity Yoneda evaluation at the identity
node.statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, and use quasicategories, mapping spaces and coherent transformations as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a $\mathcal U'$-small quasicategory and have $\mathcal U$-small mapping spaces, let $\mathcal S$ denote the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces, and let $a\in\mathcal E$. Write $h_a(x)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)$ for the coherent representable presheaf. For every coherent presheaf $P:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$, evaluation at $\operatorname{id}_a$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(h_a,P)\simeq P(a),\qquad \alpha\longmapsto\alpha_a(\operatorname{id}_a).$$
Its inverse sends $p\in P(a)$ to the coherent transformation whose component at $x$ is $f\mapsto P(f)(p)$ for $f:x\to a$. Thus for any coherent transformation $\alpha:h_a\to P$, its component maps are homotopic to $f\mapsto P(f)(\alpha_a(\operatorname{id}_a))$, coherently in $x$ and in parameters in the mapping spaces. Dually, for $Q:\mathcal E\to\mathcal S$ and $h^a(x)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(a,x)$, evaluation gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E,\mathcal S)}(h^a,Q)\simeq Q(a)$ with inverse $q\mapsto(f\mapsto Q(f)(q))$. These are equivalences of full spaces of coherent transformations, not just bijections on homotopy classes.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 8.3.1.3 (03M5), with evaluation defined in Notation 8.3.1.2 (03M4); apply also to the opposite category. Definition 5.6.6.1 (038A) gives the action on a universal element, and Theorem 5.6.6.13 (038J) supplies the coherent representable functor. Read online; not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon identifiers; no corresponding Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S'$ be the infinity category of $\mathcal U'$-small spaces, formed in a further universe. Use the coherent-nerve model $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathsf{Kan})$ defined in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. The inclusion $\iota:\mathcal S\hookrightarrow\mathcal S'$ is a full subcategory inclusion: the simplicial category of $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes has the same internal mapping complexes as the larger one, and a coherent-nerve simplex with vertices in the smaller category uses only those unchanged mapping complexes. The internal-functor and full-subcategory definitions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] then show that $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S')$ is full for every $\mathcal U'$-small $K$. Indeed, a simplex is $K\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal S'$; if each vertex functor lands in $\mathcal S$, every vertex of its domain does, so fullness makes the entire simplex factor through $\mathcal S$. Consequently the right-pinched mapping spaces between two such functors are identical in the two functor categories. This is a degreewise statement and includes empty mapping spaces.

source.place: Universe enlargement and full subcategories; explicit coherent-nerve and internal-functor definitions in the cited nodes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation] with its smaller universe equal to $\mathcal U'$ and $D=\mathcal E$. Its hypotheses hold because $\mathcal E$ is $\mathcal U'$-small. Regard $P$ as $\iota P:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S'$. The representable $j(a)$ has the same values $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)$ and coherent action as $\iota h_a$; local $\mathcal U$-smallness ensures these values lie in $\mathcal S$. The cited node gives the actual identity-evaluation map $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S')}(\iota h_a,\iota P)\simeq P(a)$, natural as an equivalence of coherent functors in the object and presheaf variables. Step 1 identifies its source with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(h_a,P)$ and leaves evaluation unchanged. This proves the contravariant assertion on full spaces. Choose a homotopy inverse $s$ of this equivalence in spaces, with its two inverse homotopies; no independent choices for individual points are needed.

source.place: Proposition 8.3.1.3 and Notation 8.3.1.2, via the existing small-category node in the enlarged universe.

proof.text:
Write $\Phi_x:\operatorname{Map}(h_x,P)\simeq P(x)$ for the coherent natural evaluation equivalences supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation] in Step 2. For $f:x\to a$, naturality in the representable variable gives
$$P(f)\big(\Phi_a(\alpha)\big)\simeq\Phi_x\big(\alpha\circ j(f)\big)=\alpha_x(f).$$
For the last equality, evaluate the composite at $\operatorname{id}_x$: the representable map $j(f):h_x\to h_a$ sends that identity to $f$ by composition with $f$. The unit homotopy gives the displayed equality in spaces. This square is the restriction of the cited natural equivalence on $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal P(\mathcal E)$, not an independently selected homotopy for each $f$. In particular, restrict it to any simplex of arrows and any simplex of the parameter space $\operatorname{Map}(h_a,P)$; its faces and degeneracies are the restrictions of that one coherent square. Setting $\alpha=s(p)$ and using the inverse homotopy $\Phi_a s\simeq\operatorname{id}$ gives the components $f\mapsto P(f)(p)$ with these coherent homotopies. The other inverse homotopy $s\Phi_a\simeq\operatorname{id}$ reconstructs every $\alpha$. Thus the formula identifies an already constructed inverse on spaces and does not attempt to assemble transformations from objectwise maps.

source.place: Universal-element action of Definition 5.6.6.1; formal naturality calculation from the coherent equivalence stated in the cited node.

proof.text:
Apply Steps 1-3 to the quasicategory $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the presheaf $Q:(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$. Its representable at $a$ is the coherent covariant representable of $\mathcal E$. To check its mapping-space values in the stated convention, use the arrow spaces $U$ and the natural pinch comparisons of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]:
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,a)\xrightarrow{\ j\ }U_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,a)=U_{\mathcal E}(a,x)^{\mathrm{op}}\xleftarrow{\ j^{\mathrm{op}}\ }\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(a,x)^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
Both arrows are homotopy equivalences; reversing a simplicial homotopy reverses its interval and exchanges the endpoints. For a Kan complex $T$, the formula $[t,(r_0,\ldots,r_n)]\mapsto[t,(r_n,\ldots,r_0)]$ gives a natural homeomorphism $|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|T|$, directly from the realization relations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. It is its own inverse and sends the realized map of a simplicial map to the same map with reversed coordinates. Thus this coherent representable is a model for $h^a(x)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(a,x)$ as a space. The coherent functor structure is the representable one on $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, so it is already supplied before this pointwise identification; one is not asserting a strict isomorphism of the two pinched models. The identity vertex remains the identity. The evaluation equivalence is consequently $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E,\mathcal S)}(h^a,Q)\simeq Q(a)$. The arrow $x\to a$ in $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $f:a\to x$ in $\mathcal E$, so Step 3 reads $q\mapsto(f\mapsto Q(f)(q))$, including its coherent naturality and both inverse homotopies.

source.place: Remark 8.3.3.6 (Hom-functor duality), with Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5), applied to the proved evaluation formula.
